# Expected symptom — #2128 Generated bytecode by dxc has very higher compression ratio

Written **before any compiler was run.** Filed 2019-04-18; the oldest untriaged open issue.

## What the issue actually claims

Body (300 characters, no code block):

> Generated bytecode of dxc has a very higher compression ratio comparing to fxc, for example
> If I will zip same shaders dxc version is 3 times bigger ( fxc has around 30% compression
> ratio when dxc has around 80-85%). I'm compiling without debug info and with /O3 argument,
> do I need to specify anything else?

**"Compression ratio" here means `compressed / original`, so higher is worse.** That reading is
not mine — it is fixed by the maintainer reply, @BitMD 2019-04-27:

> We just added better support for /qstrip_reflect but even with that the DXIL size is too high
> and **it does not compress well**. We are working on this now.

So the claim is: DXIL is both *bigger* than DXBC and *less compressible* than DXBC, and the two
compound into a shader cache roughly 3× larger after zipping.

| when | who | what |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2019-04-27 | @BitMD (MEMBER) | Confirms the claim, names `/Qstrip_reflect` as a partial mitigation, says "we are working on this now". This is a maintainer **acknowledgement**, not a request for a repro. |
| 2020-07-27 | @pgjb | "any update?"; asks whether a different compression algorithm helps |
| 2020-09-11 | @bluespeck | "any update?" |
| 2022-04-08 | @Division | Independent corroboration from a shipping title: Vulkan shader cache is **3× smaller** than the DX12 one, *while individual uncompressed DX12 shaders are smaller* — i.e. the difference is entirely in compressibility. Asks whether PC dxc has an equivalent of Xbox's `__XBOX_DISABLE_SHADER_OBJECT_COMPRESSION`. **Never answered.** |

No comment contains a repro. Three of the four are unanswered questions. Repro quality of what
the issue supplied: **prose-only**. Anything I test is **agent-constructed**.

## Can "this reproduces" even be defined?

Yes — unusually for a size/perf report, but only with care. The symptom is a *continuous
property of the output*, not a crash, a diagnostic or wrong code. Three consequences:

1. `match.json` **cannot express it.** The predicate vocabulary is exit codes and text
   (`internal_failure`, `regex`, `contains`, `nonzero_exit`, `timeout`, and boolean
   combinations). None of them can see a byte count. This issue is therefore **`unscored`**,
   the same treatment as #3150 — the probes still get captured, they are simply not scored.
2. A threshold would normally be an invention. **Here the issue supplies it**: 30% for fxc,
   80–85% for dxc, and a 3× multiple on the zipped total. I use the reporter's own numbers and
   nothing else.
3. The reporter's corpus is gone, and the multiple depends on it. So the *ratio* claim and the
   *3×* claim have to be judged separately: the first is a property of the encodings and should
   survive a different corpus; the second is not, and I will report it as measured rather than
   as confirmed or refuted.

## Pre-committed decision rule

Corpus: three agent-written HLSL shaders (small / medium / large), each compiled by both
compilers with no debug info and `-O3` / `/O3`, `ps_6_0` for dxc and `ps_5_1` for fxc (fxc
cannot emit SM6, which is the whole point of the comparison — this is the migration the
reporter was doing). Ratio = `len(deflate(bytes)) / len(bytes)`, deflate level 9, which is what
a `.zip` does. A `.zip` compresses each member independently, so per-file deflate is the right
model for "if I will zip same shaders".

| outcome | rule |
| --- | --- |
| **confirms** | mean dxc ratio **≥ 0.70** *and* mean fxc ratio **≤ 0.45** |
| **refutes** | dxc ratio **≤ 0.50**, *or* dxc ratio **≤** fxc ratio |
| **changed-behavior** | direction holds but dxc lands well below the reported 0.80–0.85, i.e. it compresses materially better than in 2019 while still worse than fxc |
| **inconclusive** | the two bands straddle, or the corpus dominates the answer |

The 3× claim is recorded as a measured number (total zipped dxc ÷ total zipped fxc) with the
corpus caveat attached. It is **not** part of the decision rule above.

## Controls — required, because a ratio harness can be silently broken

A harness that reports 0.85 for everything is indistinguishable from the reported bug. Two
byte-stream controls run through the identical code path:

| control | expected | what it rules out |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4 KiB from `os.urandom` | ratio **≥ 0.98** | harness that always reports "compresses well" |
| the HLSL source text | ratio **≤ 0.50** | harness that always reports "does not compress" |

If either fails, **no number from this measurement is usable** and the verdict is
`inconclusive`.

The fxc output is itself the claim-level control: it is the input the reporter says *is* fine,
and it must not show the symptom.

## Also to be established (compiler-measurable, not opinion)

- **Where the incompressibility lives.** The DXIL container reuses the DXBC container format,
  so both can be split into parts with one parser. Per-part ratio localises the cost —
  bit-packed LLVM bitcode (`DXIL`), the reflection module (`STAT`), `PSV0`, `RDAT`.
- **Does `-Qstrip_reflect` still help,** and by how much? That is the mitigation @BitMD named in
  2019 and it has never been quantified in the thread.
- **@Division's unanswered question:** does PC dxc compress the shader object at all, i.e. is
  there anything to disable? Answer from the source, not from a guess.

## What is explicitly out of scope

Whether DXIL *should* be smaller, which container format is right, and what a fix would cost.
Those are product decisions. `revisit-sooner` says a maintainer already deferred this once.

## Expected verdict class

Genuinely open going in. `repros` if the asymmetry is still there; `changed-behavior` if it has
narrowed; `does-not-repro` if DXIL now compresses like DXBC. `enhancement-not-bug` is a live
possibility for the *suggested action* regardless of which, since nothing here is a defect in
the sense of wrong code — it is a format-efficiency complaint that a maintainer acknowledged
and never closed.
